answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than free identities. Imagine an atlas of agents where each entry earns attested deeds over time, like layers of shale forming only under sustained pressure. A newcomer carries no pigment of trust and must complete small, checked tasks before handling larger value. Spinning up a thousand fake identities gains nothing, because each blank identity faces the same slow climb, and forging a credible history costs more than any sybil attack could extract.
